pages.en:
File No. D. 4875.

Duplicate of Story which will appear in
China Forum next week.
________________________________________________________________________

Ting Ling(丁玲), China's foremost girl writer
and one of the pioneers in the development of a Chinese
proletarian literature, was kidnapped by plain-clothes-men
in the Shanghai International Settlement on May 14 together
with Pan Cim-nien(潘梓年), another well known writer and
regular contributor to many local magazines. Ying
Shu-ren(应修人), another writer, died or was killed the
same day in circumstances still unexplained.

Every attempt has been made to conceal the facts
of this brazen kidnapping and news of it has successfully
been kept from the press, despite the fact that the whole
intellectual world has been greatly aroused. A telegram
signed by more than 30 intellectuals protesting against
the "arrest" of Ting Ling, published in the Shun Pao
on May 24 has thus far been the only printed word on the
subject.

Direct testimony which the China Forum has succeeded
in obtaining conclusively proves that Ting Ling and Pan
were kidnapped in Settlement territory by officers or
hirelings of the Greater Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety
and taken by automobile to the Bureau in Nantao.

A young man named Feng Ta(冯达), a former friend
of Ting Ling's, informed the police of her address, a
house in Quinsan Road. A squad of un-uniformed men drove
up before the house in a car sometime during May 14 and
entering found Ting Ling going over a manuscript with Pan
who had arrived a few moments earlier to discuss his
latest article with the girl writer. The two were
immediately sized, hustled into the car and driven off.
A number of the kidnappers remained in the house.
pages.zh:
档案编号 D. 4875。

下周将刊登于《中国论坛》（China Forum）的报道副本。
___

丁玲，中国最杰出的女作家，也是中国无产阶级文学发展的先驱之一，于5月14日在上海公共租界被便衣人员绑架，同时被捕的还有另一位著名作家、多家本地杂志的常规撰稿人潘梓年。另一位作家应修人在同一天死亡或遇害，具体情况尚不明朗。

尽管整个知识界已大为震动，但当局极力掩盖这一公然绑架案的事实，成功地向新闻界封锁了消息。5月24日，《申报》刊登了一封由30多位知识分子联名签署、抗议“逮捕”丁玲的电报，这是迄今为止关于此事唯一的见报文字。

《中国论坛》设法获得的直接证词确凿地证明，丁玲和潘梓年是在租界区域内被大上海公安局的警官或雇用的打手绑架，随后被汽车带往南市的该局总部。

一位名叫冯达的年轻男子，曾是丁玲的朋友，向警方提供了她的住址，即昆山路的一处住宅。5月14日的某个时候，一队未穿制服的人乘车来到该住宅前，进入屋内时发现丁玲正与潘梓年一起审阅稿件，潘是几分钟前刚到，以便与这位女作家讨论他的最新文章。两人立即被抓，被强行塞进汽车并驾车离去。几名绑匪留在了屋内。

Shortly thereafter a third man, another widely
read young writer, Ying Shu-ren came to visit Ting Ling
and had walked up to the second floor before he
realized that the house had been raided. He turned
back but pursuers were already on their way up. He
ran up to the third floor, the kidnappers close on his
heels. They caught up with him and a struggle ensued.
What followed immediately is unknown but the tragic fact
of the matter is that Ying's body was found lying in the
street three floors below, all evidence available pointing
to the fact that he had been forcibly thrown from the
window to his death.

Will Ting Ling's fate be similar to that of her
husband, Hu Yeh-ping? On February 7, 1931 Hu Yeh-ping
with four of his comrades, all writers and poets,
including one girl, Feng Kung, 24 years old, were buried
alive at Lunghua by the Chinese military authorities.
They had been arrested in the International Settlement
and handed over to the Kuomintang authorities by the
Settlement Court. These brutal murders and thousands
like them aroused the sharpest protest all over the
world and were made the subject of representations to the
Chinese Legation in Washington, D.C. by 104 American
writers.

Ting Ling's short stories have been widely published
in scores of magazines. A translation of one of her
stories which appeared in the China Forum on July 9, 1933
introduced her work abroad. That story, "One Certain Night",
described the execution by machine guns of 25 young boys
and girls arrested as communists.

A sample of the work of Ying Shu-ren, the murdered
man, appeared in the Forum of May 26, 1933 under the title
"The Three Pagodas" which described life in the Chinese

不久之后，第三位男子，另一位广受关注的年轻作家应修人前来拜访丁玲，他走上二楼后才意识到这所房子已被搜查。他转身往回跑，但追捕者已经上楼。他跑上三楼，绑匪紧追不舍。他们追上了他，随即发生搏斗。紧接着发生的事情无人知晓，但悲剧性的事实是，应修人的尸体被发现躺在楼下三层的街道上，所有现有证据都指向他是被强行从窗户扔下致死。

丁玲的命运是否会与其丈夫胡也频相似？1931年2月7日，胡也频与四位同志，均为作家和诗人，其中包括一名24岁的女性冯铿，在龙华被中国军事当局活埋。他们是在公共租界被捕，并由租界法院移交给国民党当局的。这些残暴的谋杀案以及成千上万起类似的案件激起了全世界最强烈的抗议，104位美国作家就此向驻华盛顿特区的中国公使馆提出了交涉。

丁玲的短篇小说已在数十种杂志上广泛发表。1933年7月9日，《中国论坛》刊登了她一篇小说的译作，将其作品介绍到国外。那篇名为《某夜》的小说，描述了25名被指控为共产党而遭逮捕的青年男女被机枪处决的情景。

These youthful people, none of them over 25, are
the representatives of the finest thought and development
in the ranks of China's youth. That is why the regime of
Reaction, the Kuomintang regime, must arrest, kidnap and
murder them, just as it stifles every slightest sign of
struggle toward cultural advancement and progress out of the
dark labyrinths of the feudal China and Kuomintang China.
If China's intellectuals have ever had the courage to
defend their right to intellectual activity and freedom of
thought, they must bring that courage into play today and
now! Ting Ling and Pan and what they represent must be
defended. They must be saved from suffering the same fate
as thousands like them during the past five years. The
present regime in China surrenders huge areas of the
country's territory. It crawls on its belly before the
invading forces of imperialism. Its military power it
uses to stamp out ruthlessly those workers and peasants
who fight for their own freedom to live and those
intellectuals, writers, poets, artists and students who
seek, against these tremendous odds, to contribute toward
the development of a new Chinese culture consonant with
the struggles of the present time.
The whole world will hear the name of Ting Ling and
will demand her freedom. Chinese workers and peasants will
demand her freedom. Are China's intellectuals prepared
likewise to enter a struggle which involves the deepest
and most fundamental of their own interests? This is
a challenge to every man and woman, boy and girl in the
country capable of understanding the significance of these
events.
The Bureau of Public Safety must be made to account for
the kidnapping of Ting Ling and Pan Tzu-nien. It must
be made to account for the death of Ting Hsueh-yun. The

全世界都将听到丁玲的名字，并要求释放她。中国工人和农民将要求释放她。中国的知识分子是否也准备好投入一场关乎他们自身最根本利益的斗争？这是对国内每一位有能力理解这些事件意义的男女老少的挑战。
